   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/10/russias-unfriendly-countries-list-now-targets-property-child-custody-and-debts</guid>
   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:40:07 +0100</pubDate>
   <description>Moscow’s list of states it deems unfriendly was set in March 2022 for foreign economic policy, but decrees and court rulings now apply it to child custody, vehicle registration and debt repayment.</description>

   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:37:43 +0100</pubDate>
   <description>Prince Harry and his wife Meghan visited the European Parliament in Brussels, on Tuesday 10 November, to discuss the dangers children face online. The couple met families affected by online abuse before Harry addressed the gathering.</description>

      <title>Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/lewis-hamilton-egypt-rafah-crossing-gaza-aid-facilities</link>
      <description><p>Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent</p><p>Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.</p><p>The seven-time Formula 1 world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/lewis-hamilton-egypt-rafah-crossing-gaza-aid-facilities">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives</p><p>African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.</p><p><a href="https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/see-my-world-film-festival-tickets-2000609164867">See My World</a>, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/08/african-philosophies-see-my-world-film-festival-manchester">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts">voters turning away from the party</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:46:31 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Israel live: Eisenkot party submits bill to new parliament setting up inquiry on October 7 failures</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261110-live-new-israeli-parliament-sworn-in-eisenkot-aims-to-form-government-netanyahu-knesset</link><description>
Israel's new parliament was sworn in Tuesday with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot aiming to build a coalition after receiving a mandate to form a government. Eisenkot's party moved to immediately set up a commission to investigate failures that allowed Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, a move long resisted by caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Follow our live coverage for the latest updates.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c42ebe6a-dd1d-11f1-b173-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T143111Z-351398299-RC22LOATL231-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-POLITICS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c42ebe6a-dd1d-11f1-b173-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T143111Z-351398299-RC22LOATL231-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-POLITICS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">279e7fcc-dd13-11f1-994d-05cf1ea115bd</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:40:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c42ebe6a-dd1d-11f1-b173-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T143111Z-351398299-RC22LOATL231-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-POLITICS.jpg">© Ronen Zvulun, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Entre Nous</category><title>'Clean beauty': How to navigate the latest cosmetic and skincare trends</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/entre-nous/20261110-clean-beauty-how-to-navigate-the-latest-cosmetic-and-skincare-trends</link><description>
It's hard to believe, but Christmas is just six weeks away. That means the battle of the Advent calendars is now well and truly underway. So if you love beauty products but are wanting to buy with safety and a healthy approach in mind, what do you do? Joining us from Atlanta is Lisa Fennessy, the founder and CEO of The New Knew, which reviews "clean beauty" products. She tells us what to look out for to take better care of our skin.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0cc6e0e6-dd08-11f1-87ae-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-80ef1744.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0cc6e0e6-dd08-11f1-87ae-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-80ef1744.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d3a0cd4e-dd03-11f1-a172-2f6224affb59</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:11:51 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Annette YOUNG</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Pokemon's 30-year anniversary: Japanese cards sell like wildfire</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261110-pokemon-s-30-year-anniversary-japanese-cards-sell-like-wildfire</link><description>
Pokemon, the famous Japanese little monsters, are turning 30, and their trading cards are selling like wildfire, often being flipped for small fortunes. People prepared to camp outside specialised shops in a bid to buy some of these cards.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9dc1aa64-dd0c-11f1-9fa8-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-984bb117.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9dc1aa64-dd0c-11f1-9fa8-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-984bb117.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6c3e0cc0-dd03-11f1-ad9a-5d4437a5af86</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:58:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Americas</category><title>Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls move to impeach him 'sabotage'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261110-live-pentagon-chief-pete-hegseth-calls-move-to-impeach-him-a-farce</link><description>
US ​Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday called ​moves to impeach him over abuse of power in the Iran war a farce that ​would ‌fail. The Pentagon chief slammed the move as a "political spectacle" by an outgoing congressional opponent of President Donald Trump.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a4ec11da-dd0c-11f1-9edd-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T133812Z-839619578-RC21LOABPNYD-RTRMADP-3-USA-HEGSETH.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a4ec11da-dd0c-11f1-9edd-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T133812Z-839619578-RC21LOABPNYD-RTRMADP-3-USA-HEGSETH.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">38b95690-dd0b-11f1-b081-fb8708c37a00</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:32:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a4ec11da-dd0c-11f1-9edd-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T133812Z-839619578-RC21LOABPNYD-RTRMADP-3-USA-HEGSETH.jpg">© Evelyn Hockstein, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US-mediated talks on ending Russia-Ukraine war begin in Abu Dhabi</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261110-us-mediated-talks-on-ending-russia-ukraine-war-begin-in-abu-dhabi</link><description>
Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US opened Tuesday, November 10, in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made another push to end the war. The two-day session in Abu Dhabi is the first such meeting since February. It will focus on establishing future security guarantees for the warring countries.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/121a87b4-dd03-11f1-aa06-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-46a35800.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/121a87b4-dd03-11f1-aa06-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-46a35800.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4a90e73e-dd01-11f1-891b-45ca0b05ead8</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:29:45 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description>Cholera has killed more than 3,000 people worldwide since the start of the year, the World Health Organization said on Tuesday, insisting its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remained in reach.

      <description>British children’s author and comedian David Walliams used his fame to groom girls and young women for sex, two British news outlets reported on Tuesday.
ITV News and the Guardian newspaper said they spoke with multiple women who accused Walliams of preying on them.
One woman said he sexually assaulted her when she was 15.
Walliams, 55, denied the allegations.

      <description>China hawks in Washington could weaponise allegations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence, despite denials from Beijing, Chinese experts warn.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Curiosity Mars rover sizes up new 'Nazca' dig site | Space photo of the day for Nov. 10, 2026 ]]>

NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet.

The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it.

What is it?

Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target.

MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image.

Why is it incredible?

Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow.

The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure.

The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

]]> <![CDATA[ See the first images from the new ZWO Seestar S30 Plus — a smart telescope aimed at beginners ]]> As rival makers announce increasingly ambitious smart telescopes, ZWO has taken a different approach. Its new Seestar S30 Plus launches today and will be available online from Seestar’s website and Amazon, just in time for Christmas. Better still, we’ve been using it for a month and can bring you a first look.

Announced a few months after the flagship Seestar S50 Pro and replacing the now-discontinued Seestar S30, the new Seestar S30 Plus retains its 30mm aperture and compact chassis, but upgrades to four-element apochromatic optics with extra-low dispersion (ED) glass and two 3.7-megapixel cameras.

Both produce 1,440 x 2,560-pixel images, while a much-improved 43.5-degree wide-angle camera can capture the Milky Way, constellations, star trails and nightscapes. Built-in filters, a mosaic mode and equatorial (EQ) tracking add considerable deep-sky astrophotography potential.

For a telescope weighing just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg), it’s impressive. It easily fits into a camera bag and could happily live on a bookshelf.

I’ve already photographed the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), the Pleiades (M45), the Dumbbell Nebula (M27) and the North America Nebula (NGC 7000). The results are excellent for such a small instrument, especially when imaging nebulas with its built-in dual-band filter, which helps reduce light pollution.

The Seestar app adds new in-app post-processing options, so you don’t have to mess around with any of that — though you can also export everything as lossless FITS files. The S30 Plus also includes a magnetic solar filter, enabling you to indulge in solar photography safely.

With Dwarflab’s $1,299 Draco (3.5-inch/90mm aperture) recently landed in stores and Vaonis’ own $4,990 Atlas (3.1-inch/80mm aperture) not available until 2027, ZWO’s decision to offer an upgraded entry-level smart telescope that buyers can get their hands on right now looks particularly smart.

With ZWO's pattern of delivering cheaper smart telescopes without sacrificing on quality, the Seestar S30 Plus could be one of Christmas 2026’s best gifts for anyone interested in astronomy — and maybe that’s the point of it. Either way, first impressions are good. A full review is coming tomorrow, so check back at Space.com to find out our full thoughts and testing.

]]> <![CDATA[ Total solar eclipse 2027 vs 2028 — Which one should you choose, Egypt or Australia? ]]> For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century" will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island.

Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences. The 2027 event combines over six minutes of totality with some of the very best weather prospects possible, while 2028 offers over five minutes of totality above some of the world's most famous wildernesses and cityscapes.

Eclipse chasing requires careful planning and dedication, but also significant funds. If you can only choose one, which should it be?

2027 total solar eclipse: pros and cons

On paper, 2027 is difficult to beat. Maximum totality on Aug. 2 will last about 6 minutes, 23 seconds, making it the longest totality on land since 1991 and until 2114. The path of totality will cross southern Spain and Gibraltar before sweeping across Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Somalia and the Chagos Islands. About 88.9 million people live in its path, according to Time and Date. It will dominate the news for weeks.

For Europeans, southern Spain is the obvious easy option. Tarifa, at the country's southern tip, will see about 4 minutes, 39 seconds of totality, while the U.K. Overseas Territory of Gibraltar gets about 4 minutes, 25 seconds. Travel farther east and the duration increases, with Sfax in Tunisia getting around 5 minutes, 41 seconds and locations in Egypt experiencing more than six minutes. Weather prospects generally improve, too, as the path crosses the deserts of North Africa.

Egypt is the headline destination. Luxor will see about 6 minutes, 20 seconds of totality near midday, with Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the world's greatest ancient monuments nearby. The climatic odds are excellent, with clouds extremely rare in early August. That combination of a very long totality, ancient landscapes and a very high probability of a clear sky makes 2027's path of totality highly unusual.

But there are downsides. Temperatures around Luxor can exceed 105°F (41°C) in August, a dust storm is not impossible, and totality occurs shortly after 1 p.m. when the sun (and moon) will be high overhead — making photography very difficult. Demand is already intense, making organized trips expensive. Spain will be considerably easier and probably cheaper for European eclipse chasers, but at the expense of roughly two minutes of totality — and slightly less favorable weather prospects.

2028 total solar eclipse: pros and cons

If 2027 is about extreme duration, 2028 is about choice. On July 22, 2028, a path of totality will cross the Cocos Islands, Christmas Island, Australia, from northwest to southeast — passing directly over Sydney — before continuing across the Tasman Sea to New Zealand's South Island. That's about 6.3 million people, according to Time and Date. This will be an exclusive eclipse experienced by relatively few people, certainly when compared to the eclipses in 2024, 2026 and 2027.

Maximum totality will last 5 minutes and 10 seconds in the remote Kimberley region of Western Australia. That's more than a minute shorter than 2027, but still exceptionally long by total solar eclipse standards (most last about two minutes). More importantly, the Australian Outback has excellent climatic prospects. Historical cloudiness on July 22 is around 8% at Purnululu (Bungle Bungles) close to the point of greatest eclipse in Western Australia and 19% at Karlu Karlu (Devil's Marbles) in the Northern Territory, making Australia's interior an attractive destination for serious eclipse chasers. Temperatures will be around 86°F (30°C) in July.

Then there's Sydney. Australia's largest city will experience about 3 minutes, 45 seconds of totality, its first total solar eclipse since 1857. Sydney Opera House and Harbor Bridge beneath a totally eclipsed sun could produce some of the decade's defining astronomical images, while millions of people experiencing totality together should create an extraordinary atmosphere. Temperatures will be around 62.6°F (17°C).

A compromise is weather. Historical cloudiness in Sydney is around 43%, which is good odds for most eclipses — and July is known for clear weather. But in 2028, anyone prioritizing their chances of a clear totality will be tempted by a (albeit pricier) trip to the Outback. For Europeans, reaching Australia also comes with considerable cost and time. The huge number of hotels in Sydney could keep accommodation relatively competitive, but the long flight means it makes little sense to travel there for only a few days. For many international eclipse chasers, 2028 will naturally become an expensive one- or two-week trip.

Don't forget the night sky

There's another reason to think beyond those few minutes of darkness. With the right planning, an eclipse trip can also become an extraordinary astronomy vacation (tip: come a week before the eclipse for the darkest evening skies). Here, 2028 offers visitors from Europe and North America something very different — the Southern Hemisphere night sky.

July is a superb time to see the bright central regions of the Milky Way from dark locations in Australia. The Southern Cross, or Crux, is one of the southern sky's defining sights, with Alpha and Beta Centauri nearby. Omega Centauri, the largest and brightest globular cluster visible from Earth, is another showpiece, while the Eta Carinae region offers one of the richest sections of the Milky Way for binoculars and small telescopes.

There are other reasons to extend the trip. A partial lunar eclipse occurs on July 6-7, 2028, while the Southern Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks around July 28 — a week after the eclipse, during a first-quarter moon — and is particularly well seen from the Southern Hemisphere. Add Australia's world-class dark skies, and a trip into the Outback could become as much about stargazing as the eclipse itself.

The 2027 eclipse has fewer night-sky extras. The Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks a few days before the eclipse — in dark, moonless skies — while Jupiter will dominate the western sky shortly after sunset. However, anyone traveling from the Northern Hemisphere will largely see a familiar celestial hemisphere. Australia offers a genuinely different sky experience.

City, desert or wilderness?

Perhaps the most useful way to choose between these eclipses is not to compare their durations, but to imagine where you would most like to be when the moon's shadow arrives.

In 2027, the decision largely comes down to how far along the eclipse track you want to travel. Stay in southern Spain for convenience and around four minutes of totality, head into Tunisia for longer totality and excellent weather prospects, or go all-in on Egypt for more than six minutes beneath almost cloudless desert skies — and bragging rights among eclipse chasers. It's an eclipse that can be combined with beaches, Roman ruins, North African cities or the temples and, of course, the tombs of ancient Egypt.

In 2028, the contrast is even greater. Sydney offers a communal total solar eclipse — a busy "we eclipse" — with millions watching daylight disappear above one of the world's great cities. Head thousands of miles away into the Australian interior and the same event becomes a lonely "me eclipse" in the wilderness, with up to five minutes of totality above an immense Outback landscape. Continue to New Zealand, and there's yet another possibility — a shorter totality with the sun much lower in the afternoon sky.

Which total solar eclipse should you choose?

If your priority is purely totality duration, 2027 marginally wins. More than six minutes of totality combined with extraordinarily reliable weather is a rare combination. There's a good reason Aug. 2, 2027 is being marketed as the "eclipse of the century." But if you've always wanted to visit Australia or New Zealand, the 2028 eclipse is an extraordinary excuse to finally go, in addition to experiencing a long totality.

Choose the trip you most want to take, then find the best possible place for you within the path of totality. After all, no total solar eclipse lasts long enough, and most eclipse chasers struggle to recall exactly how long totality lasted. They're just left with the same question as always — when is the next one?

For Europeans, reaching Australia also comes with considerable cost and time. There's another reason to think beyond those few minutes of darkness. With the right planning, an eclipse trip can also become an extraordinary astronomy vacation (tip: come a week before the eclipse for the darkest evening skies). Here, 2028 offers visitors from Europe and North America something very different — the Southern Hemisphere night sky.

July is a superb time to see the bright central regions of the Milky Way from dark locations in Australia. The Southern Cross, or Crux, is one of the southern sky's defining sights, with Alpha and Beta Centauri nearby. Add Australia's world-class dark skies, and a trip into the Outback could become as much about stargazing as the eclipse itself.

The 2027 eclipse has fewer night-sky extras. The Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks a few days before the eclipse — in dark, moonless skies — while Jupiter will dominate the western sky shortly after sunset. ]]> <![CDATA[ NASA's twin ESCAPADE Mars probes slingshot around Earth in unprecedented double 'gravity assist' ]]> Twin NASA spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long escapade, ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet.

The Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) spacecraft launched in November 2025 on the second-ever flight of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory. Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars.

"No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission. "For most missions, it just isn't necessary."

That's because traditionally NASA's Mars missions have been carefully choreographed within cosmic launch constraints, leaving Earth during a brief window of planetary alignment that only occurs every 26 months. ESCAPADE was meant to launch in October 2024, when Earth and Mars were favorably aligned, but delays with the New Glenn rocket forced the mission to sit out the precious launch window.

Rather than wait to launch this fall, NASA decided to try something new. ESCAPADE mission planners designed a "loitering" orbit, shaped like a kidney bean. It called for the twin probes to loop through that trajectory to be back at Earth in early November 2026, ready to continue on to Mars.

Once they arrived, however, the twin probes faced a major hurdle: Each had to perfectly execute an engine burn within Earth's gravity well. The maneuver is similar to the slingshot flybys that spacecraft regularly conduct to adjust their trajectories — but here, the probes had to fire their engines to amp up the effect of the burn rather than acting alone.

The first spacecraft tackled the feat on Nov. 7; the second did so on Monday (Nov. 9). And according to NASA, the burns went perfectly. "This is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to propel a spacecraft toward Mars, and we've now executed this maneuver twice, flawlessly, in just two days," Asal Naseri, acting associate flight director for NASA's Heliophysics Division said in a statement.

After just a few minor course corrections, ESCAPADE will be sailing toward a September 2027 Mars arrival.

A scenic detour

The twin ESCAPADE spacecraft have made the most of their extended tour. Each spacecraft is about the size of two refrigerators and equipped with three scientific instruments and a couple cameras. All are tailored for studying the strange magnetic field of Mars, which is created both globally by charged particles from the sun interacting with the atmosphere and locally by areas of highly magnetic crust.

Earth's magnetic field is much stronger and generated by the planet's core. But it too is affected by the solar wind, as scientists call the constant stream of charged particles flowing off the sun and across space. On the side of Earth opposite the sun, the solar wind stretches the magnetic field to form an elongated tail structure, like a terrestrial windsock.

A range of missions have studied this magnetotail at various points up to nearly 800,000 miles (1.27 million kilometers) away from Earth, but beyond that, it has been a mystery. Conveniently, the two ESCAPADE spacecraft traveled through the structure over the course of about 10 days early last year at a much greater distance from Earth — some 1.19 million miles (1.91 million km) away.

"We were able to capture the magnetic field structure of that distant tail, how it flaps, how it moves, how the plasma flows within it," Lillis said, gathering data that he called "unprecedented." "And not only that but for the first time, we were able to do that with two spacecraft simultaneously."

A second shot at the magnetotail came over the summer, when the spacecraft were much closer to Earth but the moon was also passing through the magnetic structure. The two ESCAPADE spacecraft were able to partner with twin ARTEMIS-THEMIS spacecraft at the moon to observe the structure from four different perspectives simultaneously.

That's a huge boon when trying to study the magnetotail and its intricate and ever-changing magnetic field lines and plasma, Lillis said. "These are generally not things you can measure remotely," he said. "You kind of have to be there."

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard ]]>

On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage.

The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight.

During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.

Why it mattered

The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon.

The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch.

NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan.

  • Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos

“It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun, director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time.

The launch came as NASA was on its heels.

Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test.

“The maiden voyage of the Saturn V dramatically increased the confidence of people across the nation in the management of the largest research and development undertaking in which the western world has ever engaged,” George Mueller, NASA's then-Associate Administrator for Manned Space Flight, said at the time.

One year later, another Saturn V rocket launched the first astronauts to the moon with the Apollo 8 mission. All of the Apollo missions that followed also launched on Saturn V rockets.

Just two years after its debut, the Saturn V rocket launched the Apollo 11 astronauts to the moon for the first crewed moon landing in July 1969.

]]> <![CDATA[ Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it ]]> Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know.

Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky. The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later.

Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker.

Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo.

Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ

The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more.

Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon.

The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches. Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts.

The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029, when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo.

Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky, along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself.

]]> <![CDATA[ Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era? ]]> Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old.

New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes, tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium.

Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole.

"A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement.

"They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added.

Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes

Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star.

"Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?"

De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots.

The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific.

"There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. "There can only be so many primordial black holes in the universe, for example, and there cannot be too many of them in a given cluster."

Considering three possible scenarios, the team found that the most likely situation is a smaller primordial black hole consuming surrounding gas and energy until it grew to be the size of QSO1.

"The door was open on this theory — that Little Red Dots could be primordial black holes," Del Grosso said. "We've now cracked it open a little farther by showing some scenarios are more likely than others."

Del Grosso and crew now intend to look at the other 100 or so Little Red Dots seen by the JWST to determine how many of them could have started life as primordial black holes.

Then scientists may finally have the evidence to say these long-theorized ancient black holes actually existed.

"We don't have a clear understanding of what happens in the early universe right after the Big Bang," De Luca concluded. "If primordial black holes do exist, then something had to happen to make them in the first place, which would be a groundbreaking discovery in physics."

The team's findings were published in June in the journal Physical Review Letters.

Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay.

That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required.

But now we have been blessed with the news, first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. ]]> <![CDATA[ Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission ]]> Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier.

The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable.

The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase.

Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher, Google's planned AI constellation).

The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site.

"This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added.

Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing, using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers.

SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections.

But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous.

"While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post.

"An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable."

The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain.

"The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said.

The Seattle company has other work to do in LEO at the moment as well: Its Otter Pup 2 prototype craft is currently gearing up to conduct a historic docking of its own in LEO.

Otter Pup 2, which launched in June 2025, has been getting closer and closer to another private spacecraft, Gilmour Space's ElaraSat. Last week, the company announced that Otter Pup 2 got within a mere 82 feet (25 meters) of its target.

"With this progress, Otter Pup 2 has officially completed Characterize, the penultimate phase of its mission. That leaves just one phase left: attempting docking, and a chance to make history," Starfish Space said in an Oct. 27 X post.

Two private satellites have docked before, but only much higher above Earth, in geostationary orbit. Such a meetup has not yet happened in LEO.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems ]]> CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners.

To build and sustain a base on the moon, NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8).

"We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them."

Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event. Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd.

The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group.

But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them.

"The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved."

"We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night. We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base.

How will it work?

This challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the U.S. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety.

This will be what Isaacman described as a "multi-phase competition that mirrors how ideas are developed actually in the aerospace industry."

"Teams will first submit concepts, then they're going to refine them, and finalists will have the opportunity to present their solutions directly to NASA leaders and stakeholders," he further explained.

"The prize money is great for sure, but the the real opportunity is to work on problems NASA is actively trying to solve right now, so students don't need to wait to graduation to contribute to that effort," Isaacman added.

A long road ahead

Right now, NASA has a long road ahead of them before a moon base is actually built. In mid-2027, the agency is planning to launch its Artemis III mission which will see a crew of four astronauts practice rendezvous maneuvers with two different lunar landers. If all goes to plan, this will be followed by Artemis IV landing humans on the moon's surface for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

The agency is making these big steps forward to not just a crewed return to the moon, but a sustained, long-term return to the moon. However, knowing that a fully-fledged moon base is still firmly in the future, they are banking on the ingenuity, creativity and passion of

If you're a student or know a student interested in participating in this challenge, you can find more information on NASA's website here. Interested students can register until Jan. 25, 2027.

 <description>Studenti Prvního českého gymnázia v Karlových Varech se zapojili do připomínky Dne válečných veteránů. Před školou vysadili makové políčko z umělých květin. Chtějí tak kolemjdoucí upozornit na tradiční sbírku a podpořit válečné veterány. Jedním z prodejních míst vlčích máků je i vrátnice gymnázia.</description>

</item>

  <item>
   <title>Místo brzdy sešlápli plyn. Jeden z řidičů trefil zastávku v Novém Boru</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/nehody/karambol-brzda-plyn-novy-bor-zastavka/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=nehody</link>
   <description>Stačila chvilka nepozornosti a z obyčejného parkování byly hned dvě dopravní nehody. Na Českolipsku se během pondělí odehrály dva podobné karamboly. Oba řidiči totiž místo brzdy sešlápli plynový pedál. Jeden z nich při manévrování v podzemních garážích naboural dvě zaparkovaná auta, druhý skončil s vozem v autobusové zastávce.</description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:20:01 +0100</pubDate>

  <item>
   <title>Kamiony už nebudou jezdit pod okny. Obchvat Svoru otevřou o několik dní dříve</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/kamiony-uz-nebudou-jezdit-pod-okny-obchvat-svoru-otevrou-o-nekolik-dni-drive/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Ředitelství silnic a dálnic tento týden otevře pro dopravu obchvat Svoru, jehož stavba začala před více než dvěma lety. Nový úsek má odvést veškerou tranzitní dopravu ze zastavěné části obce, kterou vede frekventovaná silnice I/9.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Video, které dojímá. Šimpanze odřízly záplavy, jídlo a deky mu donesl dron</title>

  <item>
   <title>Nejen mrtvá rodina, byt střelce z Polska ukrýval další hrůzy. Muž studoval vrahy</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/evropa/polsko-strelec-z-krakova-co-nasla-policie-v-byte-utocnik-se-zajimal-o-vraha-breivika/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=evropa</link>
   <description>V bytě rodiny střelce z Krakova nezahynuli jen jeho rodiče a sestra. Podle polských médií útočník zastřelil také dvě kočky. Vrah tam vypálil nejméně osmkrát, podle polských médií navíc použil tlumič. Muž, který následně v centru Krakova zabil šest lidí a další zranil, se podle polského ministra spravedlnosti Waldemara Żureka zajímal o norského teroristu Anderse Breivika.</description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:23:53 +0100</pubDate>

  <item>
   <title>Úkryt pro letadlo i usedlost. V Ralsku a Pavlovicích jsou nové kulturní památky</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/kulturni-pamatky-seznam-ochrana-mimon-pavlovice-hangar-usedlost/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Památkový fond Libereckého kraje se letos rozrostl o pět objektů, které získaly označení kulturní památka. Mezi nimi se nachází úkryt pro letadlo v Ralsku nebo socha u libereckého vlakového nádraží. Informovalo o tom pracoviště Národního památkového ústavu v Liberci (NPÚ).  </description>

    <media:description>Betonový úkryt pro proudové vojenské letadlo, takzvaný ÚL, je součástí vojenského letiště Hradčany v Ralsku. </media:description>

  <item>
   <title>Dubice slaví podzimní titul. Postup? Kluci myslí spíš na pivko, říká předseda</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/fotbal-okres/dubice-slavi-podzimni-titul-postup-kluci-mysli-spis-na-pivko-rika-predseda/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=fotbal-okres</link>
   <description>Fotbalisté dubického Spartaku zvládli podzimní derniéru, když ve Svoru vyhráli 3:1. Klub, který územně spadá pod Českou Lípu, tak nakonec v osmé lize slaví titul podzimního mistra. Doslova o prsa, jen bod totiž ztrácí druhé Zahrádky.</description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:04:00 +0100</pubDate>
   <guid>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/fotbal-okres/dubice-slavi-podzimni-titul-postup-kluci-mysli-spis-na-pivko-rika-predseda/</guid>

    <media:description>8. liga: Dubice - Mimoň B, říjen 2026</media:description>
    <media:credit>JAROSLAV MAREK</media:credit>
   </media:content>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Meteorologové vydali varování, mrznoucí déšť hrozí v části Čech i Moravy</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/predpoved-pocasi-cesko-kraje-radar-meteorologove-varovani-mrznouci-dest-namraza-snih/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=pocasi</link>
   <description>Změna počasí v Česku v některých regionech prověří chodce, silničáře i řidiče. Ještě v úterý přejde přes republiku pás deště, na severních horách se objeví sněhové vločky a místy hrozí i mrznoucí srážky. Ve středu ráno na svatého Martina to může klouzat víc. Ledovka hrozí v části Čech, ale také na západě Moravy. Další změny přinesou následující dny.</description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:22:42 +0100</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/predpoved-pocasi-cesko-kraje-radar-meteorologove-varovani-mrznouci-dest-namraza-snih/</guid>

   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/86b/86b2ad46-08b3-4328-8ebc-874475054e5a.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/86b/86b2ad46-08b3-4328-8ebc-874475054e5a.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Meteorologové varují před ledovkou na silnicích i chodnících.</media:description>
    <media:credit>DENÍK/Burda Michal</media:credit>
   </media:content>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Zimní údržbu komunikací zajistí v České Lípě poprvé městská společnost</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/zimni-udrzbu-komunikaci-ceska-lipa-mesto-technicke-sluzby/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Zimní údržbu komunikací zajistí v České Lípě poprvé městská společnost. Technické služby města Česká Lípa založila radnice v červenci 2024, údržbu komunikací převzala firma letos na jaře po skončení zimní sezony od firmy AVE, které v létě skončila smlouva.</description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 07:29:22 +0100</pubDate>
   <guid>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/zimni-udrzbu-komunikaci-ceska-lipa-mesto-technicke-sluzby/</guid>

   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/d3f/d3f5186a-eab5-4b9e-8423-9b5621fbb62e.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Správa a údržba silnic. Sypač. Ilustrační foto.</media:description>
    <media:credit>Deník/Matej Slávik</media:credit>
   </media:content>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Albert stahuje granátová jablka. Zákazníci je mohou vrátit do středy</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/albert-stahuje-granatova-jablka/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Obchodní řetězec Albert upozornil na problém u jedné šarže BIO granátových jablek. Ovoce stáhl z prodeje a zákazníky vyzval, aby ho vrátili. Na vrácení mají čas do středy.</description>

    <media:description>Albert stahuje z granátová jablka. Ilustrační foto.</media:description>
    <media:credit>Deník/Tomáš Ondra</media:credit>
   </media:content>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Skupina Holki převlékla své hity. A proč jedna z nich zatrhla dceři instagram?</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/mimo-roli/skupina-holki-prevlekla-sve-hity-a-proc-jedna-z-nich-zatrhla-dceri-instagram/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=mimo-roli</link>
   <description>Skupina Holki vydala album Desetkrát, na němž známé hity doprovází živá kapela.     <item>
      <title>Klempíř se kritikům mstí, míní protestující. Obavy mají o svobodu médií i kultury</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/studenti-demonstrace-na-podporu-verejnopravnich-medii.A261110_080537_domaci_jira#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Vysokoškolští studenti dnes opět protestují proti změně financování veřejnoprávních médií. Akce se konají v Praze i dalších městech, v metropoli vyvrcholí v symbolických 16:36 hodin demonstrací na náměstí Republiky, kam dorazily jednotlivé průvody. Promluví zástupci jednotlivých vysokých škol a vystoupí i studentské kapely. </description>
      <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:50:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci">Zprávy - Domácí</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/studenti-demonstrace-na-podporu-verejnopravnich-medii.A261110_080537_domaci_jira/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261110_080537_domaci_jira</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/112/cl6/ASU8b327cdc5a_162903_4501297.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Setkání studentů na podporu veřejnoprávních médií, pořádá iniciativa Vstávej techniko! Pochod přes Letenskou pláň na náměstí Republiky na celopražskou akci v 16:36, kde se konal studentský protest proti vládnímu návrhu na zrušení televizních a rozhlasových poplatků a začlenění financování veřejnoprávních médií do státního rozpočtu. (10. listopadu 2026)</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Havlíček přivezl na Ukrajinu nejpočetnější českou delegaci. Nechybějí známé firmy</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/havlicek-cesta-na-ukrajinu-delegace-prilet.A261110_163204_domaci_ijan#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Od našich zpravodajů na Ukrajině – První místopředseda vlády a ministr průmyslu a obchodu Karel Havlíček (ANO) dorazil na Ukrajinu. „Mám s členy ukrajinské vlády velmi dobré vztahy. Jedna z nejvlivnějších postav ukrajinské politiky, Denys Šmyhal, nám pomáhala připravit program na míru. Budeme na několika místech, bude to logisticky nejnáročnější návštěva,“ řekl iDNES.cz vicepremiér. Delegace, která Havlíčka doprovází, čítá na 100 lidí, převážně podnikatelů.</description>
      <pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:48:00 GMT</pubDate>

<item>
 <title>O vztahu ředitele Nvidie s čínskou špionkou nevíme všechno, říká Jonáš. Situace je podle něj vážná</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/o-vztahu-reditele-nvidie-s-cinskou-spionkou-nevime-vsechno-rika-jonas-situace-je_2611101316_tez</link>
 <description>Spojené státy americké prověřují okolnosti vztahu mezi ředitelem společnosti Nvidia Jensenem Huangem a ženou podezřelou ze špionáže pro Čínu. Aféra otřásla americkou politickou scénou i technologickým odvětvím. Zpravodajci začali ženu sledovat před více než rokem kvůli podezření, že její firma nelegálně pašuje mikroprocesory do Číny. „Jedná se o vážnou situaci,“ říká pro Radiožurnál česko-americký investiční bankéř Ondřej Jonáš.</description>

<description>Česká národní banka (ČNB) otestovala obchodování s vlastními dluhopisy prostřednictvím technologie, která je spojená předev&#353;ím s bitcoinem a dal&#353;ími kryptoměnami. Liberecký kraj proto vyzval polské velvyslanectví i železničáře k urychlení oprav a opatřením proti krádežím.</description></item><item><title>Výsledek voleb v Liberci platí. Soud zamítl stížnost, zastupitelé usednou 19. listopadu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905350-soud-zamitl-navrh-na-neplatnost-hlasovani-ve-volbach-v-liberci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905350-soud-zamitl-navrh-na-neplatnost-hlasovani-ve-volbach-v-liberci.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 18:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Soud v pondělí 9. listopadu zamítl návrh na neplatnost hlasování v komunálních volbách v Liberci. Návrh končícího náměstka primátora Adama Lenerta (ANO) byl založen jen na statistických odchylkách, soud ho odmítl jako nedůvodný, vyplývá z rozhodnutí na úřední desce pobočky krajského soudu v Liberci.</description></item><item><title>Liberecké gymnastky září. Z MČR vezou stříbro, doma vybojovaly dvě zlata</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/905310-liberecke-gymnastky-zari-z-mcr-vezou-stribro-doma-vybojovaly-dve-zlata.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/905310-liberecke-gymnastky-zari-z-mcr-vezou-stribro-doma-vybojovaly-dve-zlata.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 18:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Ostatní sporty</category><description>Podzimní závodní sezona je v plném proudu a gymnastky z oddílu Sportovní gymnastika Liberec mají za sebou další úspěšná vystoupení. Na mistrovství České republiky v Lounech získaly stříbrnou medaili, na domácím Ještědském poháru přidaly dvě vítězství. A další důležité závody je čekají.</description></item><item><title>Pohyb s dětmi v městském provozu? Dopravní podnik pozval preventisty z celého Česka</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905075-pohyb-s-detmi-v-mestskem-provozu-dopravni-podnik-pozval-preventisty-z-celeho-ceska.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905075-pohyb-s-detmi-v-mestskem-provozu-dopravni-podnik-pozval-preventisty-z-celeho-ceska.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Na šest desítek policejních preventistů přišlo do libereckého dopravního podniku. Důvod? Aby si na vlastní kůži vyzkoušeli a osahali, jak se pohybovat v blízkosti zastávek MHD, autobusů a tramvají. Své zkušenosti pak předají ve školách a školkách.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:47:57 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.4 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Vítr z hor – Tobias Piero Dohm: RAUM – ZEIT https://www.vybezek.eu/296639-vitr-z-hor-tobias-piero-dohm-raum-zeit/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:47:57 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296639 V pondělí 9. listopadu 2026 byl zahájen letošní ročník divadelního festivalu Vítr z hor, jako první se představil performer Tobias Piero Dohm v představení RAUM – ZEIT.

Z anotací – Festival Vítr z hor se i letos připojuje k mezinárodní akci La Nuit du Cirque, a přináší do Šluknovského výběžku cirkusový vír fantazie, odvahy a hravosti. A co vás čeká?

Kromě tří dnů Cirkusových nocí 13. – 15. 11. i dvě další novocirkusová představení 9. a 12. listopadu! Nenechte si je ujít! V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 Tobias Piero Dohm (@pieroodo): Raum Zeit. Vizuálně působivá inscenace, v níž se pohybem, objekty a proměnlivým prostorem posouvají hranice mezi tělem, prostředím a časem.

Tma, kouř, koule. Koule skoro všude. A písek…

]]> Festival rostlin v České Kamenici https://www.vybezek.eu/296611-festival-rostlin-v-ceske-kamenici/ Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:26:06 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296611 V sobotu 7. a neděli 8. listopadu 2026 se ve sportovní hale v České Kamenici koná Festival rostlin.

Akce, která pokud vím, tu dosud neměla obdoby. Celá hala plná několika řad regálů a na nich kytky, spousty kytek. Mnohdy takových, jaké jste ještě nejspíš ani neviděli… A davy, odnášející si mnohdy nejednu plnou tašku. Neuvěřitelný výběr. Plus nějaké doplňky.

Pro mne zjištění, že jsem uvázl v minulosti a jsem mimo nejen v náhledu na ceny v restauracích, ale zaspal jsem i cenový vývoj u pokojovek. Vlastně hrůza, jak velké jmění mi za pár let doma různě uschlo…

]]> Parní vlak na trase Drážďany – Moldava a zpět 07. 11. 2026 https://www.vybezek.eu/296569-parni-vlak-na-trase-drazdany-moldava-a-zpet-07-11-2026/ Sat, 07 Nov 2026 13:57:39 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296569 V sobotu 7. listopadu 2026 za hojného zájmu přihlížejících dětí, dospělých i šotoušů zastavila na vlakovém nádraží v Rumburku zase jednou souprava tažená parní lokomotivou (35 1097).

Žst. Rumburk:

Moldavská dráha / Teplický Semmering / „Most – Freiberg“ na FB:

V SOBOTU 7. LISTOPADU VYRAZÍ Z DRÁŽĎAN PARNÍ VLAK NA MOLDAVU!

Železniční muzeum Dresden-Altstadt a spolek Flügelradtouristik pořádají mimořádnou jízdu historického vlaku s oddílovými osobními vozy a jídelním vozem.

Z Drážďan vyrazí v 6:30 s německou parní lokomotivou 35 1097 přes Rumburk a Děčín do Mostu. Zde převezme vlak česká parní lokomotiva 433.001 „Skaličák“, které bude na horské trati pomáhat dieselová lokomotiva.

Most 12:00 – Osek město 12:32 – Dubí 13:22 – Moldava 14:09. Zpět z Moldavy vlak odjede v 15:20 přes Dubí, Louku u Litvínova a Teplice do Drážďan. Část historické soupravy zamíří také do Žatce, města chmele a piva.

Souprava na nádraží doplnila vodu (výpomoc poskytly dva vozy JSDH Brtníky), a posádka provedla na mašině nutný servis (trochu mne zaskočily dva pytle písku, ale má to logické vysvětlení).

Na FB Děčínsko video a info:

Parní vlak v čele s německou lokomotivou 35 1097-1 (vyrobenou v roce 1959 a známou také pod přezdívkou Rübezahl) projel v sobotu dopoledne těsně před desátou hodinou po železničním mostě mezi Děčínem východ a hlavním nádražím. Pohled na tuto historickou soupravu z nové lávky pro pěší a cyklisty.
